proof: Concurrent duplicate submission binds Idempotency-Key to the canonical scoped request digest and returns one durable inbox entry.
Concurrent processors use bounded PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims and create one DatasetVersion and one handoff per evidence record.
Changed payloads under a reused Idempotency-Key or evidence ID fail closed with HTTP 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
Cross-tenant and cross-user reads return the scoped absence semantics, and failed extraction records remain available through the scoped DLQ and replay path.
The scoped evidence digest deterministically binds the inbox record, stable dataset_version_id, and one Observe/Learn-only handoff.
Acknowledgement requires the exact dataset_version_id and digest, then persists one acknowledgement_id without creating runtime, deployment, broker, or capital authority.
PostgreSQL integration tests prove an expired processing lease is reclaimed by a new worker after interruption and the stale lease token cannot commit.
The schema-migration test upgrades prior global primary keys to tenant/user-scoped keys while preserving recoverable inbox state.
Lease-token comparison rejects stale completion, leaving the current owner as the only writer of processed or failed state.
Stable request digests and one-time acknowledgement make replay compensating and idempotent instead of duplicating DatasetVersion or handoff effects.
